#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every table and chart in Life, Compiled, computed from the canonical sources.

The residue-to-mark map and the 64-codon table are read out of Vox's
genetic_table.rs, which is where they live. Every word, pairing and verdict comes
from the vox binary, not from a rule restated here. Run from this directory:

    python3 make_tables.py

It writes tab_codons.tex, tab_letters.tex, tab_folds.tex, tab_exe.tex,
tab_mtco1.tex and dat_hist.tex, which life_compiled.tex inputs.
"""
import re, subprocess, collections, pathlib

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent                      # ~/imsgct
VOX = ROOT / "Vox" / "target" / "release" / "vox"
TABLE_RS = ROOT / "Vox" / "src" / "genetic_table.rs"

# ── the canonical maps, read out of the instrument's own source ──────────────

src = TABLE_RS.read_text()

CODONS = {}                                    # "AUG" -> ("aa","Met") | ("stop",...)
for cod, kind, val in re.findall(r'\("([ACGU]{3})",\s*"(\w+)",\s*"(\w+)"\)', src):
    CODONS[cod] = (kind, val)
assert len(CODONS) == 64, len(CODONS)

MARK = {}                                      # "Met" -> ("⊢","Dimensionality",0)
for aa, gl, axis, slot in re.findall(r'\("(\w{3})",\s*\'(.)\',\s*"(\w+)",\s*(\d+)\)', src):
    MARK[aa] = (gl, axis, int(slot))
assert len(MARK) == 12, len(MARK)

# The eight the third base cannot disturb carry no mark. Naming them here is
# reading the code, not choosing: they are the residues no promoted mark claims.
SCAFFOLD = sorted({v for k, v in CODONS.values() if k == "aa"} - set(MARK))

BASES = "UCAG"


def vox(*args):
    r = subprocess.run([str(VOX), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout


def tex_mark(g):
    return "\\mk{%s}" % g if g else ""


# ── 1. the complete code, all sixty-four codons ─────────────────────────────

def codon_table():
    rows = []
    for b1 in BASES:
        for b2 in BASES:
            box = [CODONS[b1 + b2 + b3] for b3 in BASES]
            names = {v for k, v in box}
            exact = len(names) == 1
            cells = []
            for kind, val in box:
                if kind == "stop":
                    cells.append("\\textit{stop}")
                elif val in MARK:
                    cells.append("%s\\,%s" % (tex_mark(MARK[val][0]), val))
                else:
                    cells.append("\\textcolor{black!45}{%s}" % val)
            rows.append((b1 + b2, exact, cells))
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{longtable}{c c llll}",
           "\\caption[The whole code, read]{Every codon of the standard code with the "
           "letter it emits. A box is \\emph{exact} when its four third-base variants "
           "imscribe one residue, and the exactness is computed from the values of the "
           "first two bases rather than looked up. The eight residues in grey carry no "
           "mark: they occupy exact boxes and the reading passes over them. Three "
           "codons assign no residue at all.}\\label{tab:codons}\\\\",
           "\\toprule",
           "box & third base & U & C & A & G \\\\",
           "\\midrule", "\\endfirsthead",
           "\\toprule box & third base & U & C & A & G \\\\ \\midrule \\endhead",
           "\\bottomrule \\endlastfoot"]
    for name, exact, cells in rows:
        out.append("\\texttt{%s\\textperiodcentered} & %s & %s \\\\" % (
            name, "exact" if exact else "split", " & ".join(cells)))
    out.append("\\end{longtable}")
    n_exact = sum(1 for _, e, _ in rows if e)
    return "\n".join(out), n_exact


# ── 2. the twelve letters, with their axes and their codons ─────────────────

def letters_table():
    OP = {
        "Met": "opens the reading", "Trp": "closes the reading",
        "His": "refers to itself", "Asn": "divides", "Gln": "rejoins",
        "Cys": "carries forward", "Tyr": "carries back", "Phe": "composes",
        "Ile": "tests on the true axis", "Asp": "tests on the false axis",
        "Lys": "tests on the information axis", "Glu": "holds a fixed point",
    }
    CHEM = {
        "Met": "initiator tRNA, formyl removed", "Trp": "buried indole",
        "His": "imidazole at the cell's pH", "Asn": "sequon, branched glycan",
        "Gln": "isopeptide acyl donor", "Cys": "disulfide",
        "Tyr": "phenol, proton and phosphate", "Phe": "aromatic stacking",
        "Ile": "$\\beta$-branched, strand", "Asp": "short carboxylate, salt bridge",
        "Lys": "$\\varepsilon$-amine, written on", "Glu": "carboxylate, held charge",
    }
    order = sorted(MARK, key=lambda a: MARK[a][2])
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{center}", "\\small",
           "\\begin{tabular}{clllll}", "\\toprule",
           "Letter & Axis & Operation & Residue & Codons & In the chain \\\\",
           "\\midrule"]
    for aa in order:
        gl, axis, slot = MARK[aa]
        cods = sorted(c for c, (k, v) in CODONS.items() if v == aa)
        out.append("%s & %s & %s & %s & \\texttt{%s} & %s \\\\" % (
            tex_mark(gl), axis, OP[aa], aa, ", ".join(cods), CHEM[aa]))
    out += ["\\midrule",
            "\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize The eight that carry no mark: %s. "
            "Three codons assign no residue.}\\\\" % ", ".join(SCAFFOLD),
            "\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}", "\\end{center}"]
    return "\n".join(out)


# ── 3. every fold of the sweep ──────────────────────────────────────────────

def folds_table():
    rows, seen = [], set()
    for line in (HERE / "pdb_fold_sweep.tsv").read_text().splitlines()[1:]:
        f = line.split("\t")
        if len(f) < 4 or not f[3].strip():
            continue
        verdict, promoted, name, word = f[0], int(f[1]), f[2], f[3].strip()
        if (name, word) in seen:
            continue
        seen.add((name, word))
        p = vox("pairs", word)
        reg = int(re.search(r"regions\s+(\d+) paired, (\d+) substantial", p).group(1))
        sub = int(re.search(r"regions\s+(\d+) paired, (\d+) substantial", p).group(2))
        una = int(re.search(r"unanswered\s+(\d+)", p).group(1))
        uno = int(re.search(r"unopened\s+(\d+)", p).group(1))
        v = re.search(r"verdict\s+(\w)", p).group(1)
        rows.append(dict(name=name.replace(".pdb", "").replace("_", "\\_"),
                         n=len(word), promoted=promoted,
                         fork=word.count("∈"), fuse=word.count("∋"),
                         reg=reg, sub=sub, una=una, uno=uno, v=v))
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{longtable}{lrrrrrrrc}",
           "\\caption[Every fold of the sweep]{The whole sweep, one row per "
           "sequence-bearing structure. The word's length, its divisions and "
           "rejoinings, the regions the pairing forms and how many of them hold "
           "work, what is left unanswered or unopened, and the reading. The sign of "
           "$d = \\lvert\\in\\rvert - \\lvert\\ni\\rvert$ decides both failures and "
           "nothing else in the row is consulted for them.}\\label{tab:folds}\\\\",
           "\\toprule",
           "structure & letters & $\\in$ & $\\ni$ & $d$ & regions & work & open & "
           "unopened & reading \\\\",
           "\\midrule", "\\endfirsthead",
           "\\toprule structure & letters & $\\in$ & $\\ni$ & $d$ & regions & work & "
           "open & unopened & reading \\\\ \\midrule \\endhead",
           "\\bottomrule \\endlastfoot"]
    key = {"T": 0, "B": 1, "F": 2, "N": 3}
    NAME = {"T": "closes", "B": "hangs open", "F": "ill-typed", "N": "null"}
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (key[r["v"]], -r["n"])):
        out.append("%s & %d & %d & %d & %+d & %d & %d & %d & %d & %s \\\\" % (
            r["name"], r["n"], r["fork"], r["fuse"], r["fork"] - r["fuse"],
            r["reg"], r["sub"], r["una"], r["uno"], NAME[r["v"]]))
    out.append("\\end{longtable}")
    return "\n".join(out), rows


# ── 4. the executable lane, every binary read the same way ──────────────────

BINARIES = [
    ("/bin/ls", "the file lister"),
    ("/bin/dash", "a shell"),
    ("/usr/bin/gzip", "a compressor"),
    ("/mnt/e/Windows/System32/Magnify.exe", "a Windows accessory"),
]


def exe_table():
    rows = []
    for path, gloss in BINARIES:
        if not pathlib.Path(path).exists():
            continue
        words = [l.split("\t")[1] for l in vox("word", path).splitlines()
                 if "\t" in l]
        tal = collections.Counter()
        ds = collections.Counter()
        for w in words:
            tal[vox("verdict", w).strip().split()[-1]] += 1
            ds[w.count("∈") - w.count("∋")] += 1
        rows.append((path, gloss, len(words), tal, ds))
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{center}", "\\small", "\\begin{tabular}{llrrrrr}", "\\toprule",
           "binary & & functions & closes & hangs open & ill-typed & null \\\\",
           "\\midrule"]
    for path, gloss, n, tal, _ in rows:
        out.append("\\texttt{%s} & \\footnotesize %s & %d & %d & %d & %d & %d \\\\" % (
            path.split("/")[-1], gloss, n, tal["T"], tal["B"], tal["F"], tal["N"]))
    out += ["\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}", "\\end{center}"]
    return "\n".join(out), rows


# ── 5. the worked example, whole ────────────────────────────────────────────

MTCO1 = HERE / "mt_co1.txt"


def mtco1_table():
    seq = MTCO1.read_text().strip()
    r = vox("rna", seq, "--dialect", "mito")
    word = re.search(r"^word\s+(\S+)", r, re.M).group(1)
    stop = re.search(r"^stop\s+(\S+)", r, re.M).group(1)
    p = vox("pairs", word)
    regions = []
    for line in p.splitlines():
        f = line.split()
        if len(f) >= 4 and f[0].isdigit():
            regions.append((int(f[0]), int(f[1]), int(f[2]), f[3],
                            f[4] if len(f) > 4 else ""))
    una = re.search(r"unanswered\s+(\d+) division\(s\) at (\S+)", p)
    grid = []
    for i in range(0, len(word), 32):
        chunk = word[i:i + 32]
        grid.append("\\texttt{\\scriptsize %3d}~~%s" % (
            i, "".join("\\mk{%s}" % c for c in chunk)))
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{center}\\small",
           "\\begin{tabular}{l@{\\hskip 1.2em}l}", "\\toprule",
           "\\multicolumn{2}{l}{\\textsc{mt-co1}, the whole word, "
           "%d letters, offset every thirty-two} \\\\" % len(word),
           "\\midrule"]
    for i in range(0, len(grid), 2):
        pair = grid[i:i + 2]
        out.append(" & ".join(pair) + (" & " if len(pair) == 1 else "") + "\\\\")
    out += ["\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}", "\\end{center}",
            "", "\\begin{center}\\small",
            "\\begin{tabular}{rrrcl}", "\\toprule",
            "opens & closes & span & work & what stands between \\\\", "\\midrule"]
    for s, f, span, w, inner in regions:
        out.append("%d & %d & %d & %s & %s \\\\" % (
            s, f, span, w, "".join("\\mk{%s}" % c for c in inner)))
    out += ["\\midrule",

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every table and chart in Life, Compiled, computed from the canonical sources.

The residue-to-mark map and the 64-codon table are read out of Vox's
genetic_table.rs, which is where they live. Every word, pairing and verdict comes
from the vox binary, not from a rule restated here. Run from this directory:

    python3 make_tables.py

It writes tab_codons.tex, tab_letters.tex, tab_folds.tex, tab_exe.tex,
tab_mtco1.tex and dat_hist.tex, which life_compiled.tex inputs.
"""
import re, subprocess, collections, pathlib

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent                      # ~/imsgct
VOX = ROOT / "Vox" / "target" / "release" / "vox"
TABLE_RS = ROOT / "Vox" / "src" / "genetic_table.rs"

# ── the canonical maps, read out of the instrument's own source ──────────────

src = TABLE_RS.read_text()

CODONS = {}                                    # "AUG" -> ("aa","Met") | ("stop",...)
for cod, kind, val in re.findall(r'\("([ACGU]{3})",\s*"(\w+)",\s*"(\w+)"\)', src):
    CODONS[cod] = (kind, val)
assert len(CODONS) == 64, len(CODONS)

MARK = {}                                      # "Met" -> ("⊢","Dimensionality",0)
for aa, gl, axis, slot in re.findall(r'\("(\w{3})",\s*\'(.)\',\s*"(\w+)",\s*(\d+)\)', src):
    MARK[aa] = (gl, axis, int(slot))
assert len(MARK) == 12, len(MARK)

# The eight the third base cannot disturb carry no mark. Naming them here is
# reading the code, not choosing: they are the residues no promoted mark claims.
SCAFFOLD = sorted({v for k, v in CODONS.values() if k == "aa"} - set(MARK))

BASES = "UCAG"


def vox(*args):
    r = subprocess.run([str(VOX), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout


def tex_mark(g):
    return "\\mk{%s}" % g if g else ""


# ── 1. the complete code, all sixty-four codons ─────────────────────────────

def codon_table():
    rows = []
    for b1 in BASES:
        for b2 in BASES:
            box = [CODONS[b1 + b2 + b3] for b3 in BASES]
            names = {v for k, v in box}
            exact = len(names) == 1
            cells = []
            for kind, val in box:
                if kind == "stop":
                    cells.append("\\textit{stop}")
                elif val in MARK:
                    cells.append("%s\\,%s" % (tex_mark(MARK[val][0]), val))
                else:
                    cells.append("\\textcolor{black!45}{%s}" % val)
            rows.append((b1 + b2, exact, cells))
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{longtable}{c c llll}",
           "\\caption[The whole code, read]{Every codon of the standard code with the "
           "letter it emits. A box is \\emph{exact} when its four third-base variants "
           "imscribe one residue, and the exactness is computed from the values of the "
           "first two bases rather than looked up. The eight residues in grey carry no "
           "mark: they occupy exact boxes and the reading passes over them. Three "
           "codons assign no residue at all.}\\label{tab:codons}\\\\",
           "\\toprule",
           "box & third base & U & C & A & G \\\\",
           "\\midrule", "\\endfirsthead",
           "\\toprule box & third base & U & C & A & G \\\\ \\midrule \\endhead",
           "\\bottomrule \\endlastfoot"]
    for name, exact, cells in rows:
        out.append("\\texttt{%s\\textperiodcentered} & %s & %s \\\\" % (
            name, "exact" if exact else "split", " & ".join(cells)))
    out.append("\\end{longtable}")
    n_exact = sum(1 for _, e, _ in rows if e)
    return "\n".join(out), n_exact


# ── 2. the twelve letters, with their axes and their codons ─────────────────

def letters_table():
    OP = {
        "Met": "opens the reading", "Trp": "closes the reading",
        "His": "refers to itself", "Asn": "divides", "Gln": "rejoins",
        "Cys": "carries forward", "Tyr": "carries back", "Phe": "composes",
        "Ile": "tests on the true axis", "Asp": "tests on the false axis",
        "Lys": "tests on the information axis", "Glu": "holds a fixed point",
    }
    CHEM = {
        "Met": "initiator tRNA, formyl removed", "Trp": "buried indole",
        "His": "imidazole at the cell's pH", "Asn": "sequon, branched glycan",
        "Gln": "isopeptide acyl donor", "Cys": "disulfide",
        "Tyr": "phenol, proton and phosphate", "Phe": "aromatic stacking",
        "Ile": "$\\beta$-branched, strand", "Asp": "short carboxylate, salt bridge",
        "Lys": "$\\varepsilon$-amine, written on", "Glu": "carboxylate, held charge",
    }
    order = sorted(MARK, key=lambda a: MARK[a][2])
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{center}", "\\small",
           "\\begin{tabular}{clllll}", "\\toprule",
           "Letter & Axis & Operation & Residue & Codons & In the chain \\\\",
           "\\midrule"]
    for aa in order:
        gl, axis, slot = MARK[aa]
        cods = sorted(c for c, (k, v) in CODONS.items() if v == aa)
        out.append("%s & %s & %s & %s & \\texttt{%s} & %s \\\\" % (
            tex_mark(gl), axis, OP[aa], aa, ", ".join(cods), CHEM[aa]))
    out += ["\\midrule",
            "\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize The eight that carry no mark: %s. "
            "Three codons assign no residue.}\\\\" % ", ".join(SCAFFOLD),
            "\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}", "\\end{center}"]
    return "\n".join(out)


# ── 3. every fold of the sweep ──────────────────────────────────────────────

def folds_table():
    rows, seen = [], set()
    for line in (HERE / "pdb_fold_sweep.tsv").read_text().splitlines()[1:]:
        f = line.split("\t")
        if len(f) < 4 or not f[3].strip():
            continue
        verdict, promoted, name, word = f[0], int(f[1]), f[2], f[3].strip()
        if (name, word) in seen:
            continue
        seen.add((name, word))
        p = vox("pairs", word)
        reg = int(re.search(r"regions\s+(\d+) paired, (\d+) substantial", p).group(1))
        sub = int(re.search(r"regions\s+(\d+) paired, (\d+) substantial", p).group(2))
        una = int(re.search(r"unanswered\s+(\d+)", p).group(1))
        uno = int(re.search(r"unopened\s+(\d+)", p).group(1))
        v = re.search(r"verdict\s+(\w)", p).group(1)
        rows.append(dict(name=name.replace(".pdb", "").replace("_", "\\_"),
                         n=len(word), promoted=promoted,
                         fork=word.count("∈"), fuse=word.count("∋"),
                         reg=reg, sub=sub, una=una, uno=uno, v=v))
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{longtable}{lrrrrrrrc}",
           "\\caption[Every fold of the sweep]{The whole sweep, one row per "
           "sequence-bearing structure. The word's length, its divisions and "
           "rejoinings, the regions the pairing forms and how many of them hold "
           "work, what is left unanswered or unopened, and the reading. The sign of "
           "$d = \\lvert\\in\\rvert - \\lvert\\ni\\rvert$ decides both failures and "
           "nothing else in the row is consulted for them.}\\label{tab:folds}\\\\",
           "\\toprule",
           "structure & letters & $\\in$ & $\\ni$ & $d$ & regions & work & open & "
           "unopened & reading \\\\",
           "\\midrule", "\\endfirsthead",
           "\\toprule structure & letters & $\\in$ & $\\ni$ & $d$ & regions & work & "
           "open & unopened & reading \\\\ \\midrule \\endhead",
           "\\bottomrule \\endlastfoot"]
    key = {"T": 0, "B": 1, "F": 2, "N": 3}
    NAME = {"T": "closes", "B": "hangs open", "F": "ill-typed", "N": "null"}
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (key[r["v"]], -r["n"])):
        out.append("%s & %d & %d & %d & %+d & %d & %d & %d & %d & %s \\\\" % (
            r["name"], r["n"], r["fork"], r["fuse"], r["fork"] - r["fuse"],
            r["reg"], r["sub"], r["una"], r["uno"], NAME[r["v"]]))
    out.append("\\end{longtable}")
    return "\n".join(out), rows


# ── 4. the executable lane, every binary read the same way ──────────────────

BINARIES = [
    ("/bin/ls", "the file lister"),
    ("/bin/dash", "a shell"),
    ("/usr/bin/gzip", "a compressor"),
    ("/mnt/e/Windows/System32/Magnify.exe", "a Windows accessory"),
]


def exe_table():
    rows = []
    for path, gloss in BINARIES:
        if not pathlib.Path(path).exists():
            continue
        words = [l.split("\t")[1] for l in vox("word", path).splitlines()
                 if "\t" in l]
        tal = collections.Counter()
        ds = collections.Counter()
        for w in words:
            tal[vox("verdict", w).strip().split()[-1]] += 1
            ds[w.count("∈") - w.count("∋")] += 1
        rows.append((path, gloss, len(words), tal, ds))
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{center}", "\\small", "\\begin{tabular}{llrrrrr}", "\\toprule",
           "binary & & functions & closes & hangs open & ill-typed & null \\\\",
           "\\midrule"]
    for path, gloss, n, tal, _ in rows:
        out.append("\\texttt{%s} & \\footnotesize %s & %d & %d & %d & %d & %d \\\\" % (
            path.split("/")[-1], gloss, n, tal["T"], tal["B"], tal["F"], tal["N"]))
    out += ["\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}", "\\end{center}"]
    return "\n".join(out), rows


# ── 5. the worked example, whole ────────────────────────────────────────────

MTCO1 = HERE / "mt_co1.txt"


def mtco1_table():
    seq = MTCO1.read_text().strip()
    r = vox("rna", seq, "--dialect", "mito")
    word = re.search(r"^word\s+(\S+)", r, re.M).group(1)
    stop = re.search(r"^stop\s+(\S+)", r, re.M).group(1)
    p = vox("pairs", word)
    regions = []
    for line in p.splitlines():
        f = line.split()
        if len(f) >= 4 and f[0].isdigit():
            regions.append((int(f[0]), int(f[1]), int(f[2]), f[3],
                            f[4] if len(f) > 4 else ""))
    una = re.search(r"unanswered\s+(\d+) division\(s\) at (\S+)", p)
    grid = []
    for i in range(0, len(word), 32):
        chunk = word[i:i + 32]
        grid.append("\\texttt{\\scriptsize %3d}~~%s" % (
            i, "".join("\\mk{%s}" % c for c in chunk)))
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{center}\\small",
           "\\begin{tabular}{l@{\\hskip 1.2em}l}", "\\toprule",
           "\\multicolumn{2}{l}{\\textsc{mt-co1}, the whole word, "
           "%d letters, offset every thirty-two} \\\\" % len(word),
           "\\midrule"]
    for i in range(0, len(grid), 2):
        pair = grid[i:i + 2]
        out.append(" & ".join(pair) + (" & " if len(pair) == 1 else "") + "\\\\")
    out += ["\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}", "\\end{center}",
            "", "\\begin{center}\\small",
            "\\begin{tabular}{rrrcl}", "\\toprule",
            "opens & closes & span & work & what stands between \\\\", "\\midrule"]
    for s, f, span, w, inner in regions:
        out.append("%d & %d & %d & %s & %s \\\\" % (
            s, f, span, w, "".join("\\mk{%s}" % c for c in inner)))
    out += ["\\midrule",
            "\\multicolumn{5}{l}{\\footnotesize %s unanswered divisions, at letters "
            "%s. Reading stops at \\texttt{%s}.}\\\\" % (
                una.group(1), una.group(2).replace(",", ", "), stop),
            "\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular}", "\\end{center}"]
    return "\n".join(out), word, regions


# ── 6. the distribution of d, both corpora, every value ─────────────────────

def hist(folds, exes):
    def bars(counter, colour, y0, scale, label):
        lo, hi = min(counter), max(counter)
        keys = [k for k in range(lo, hi + 1)]
        w = 11.6 / max(len(keys), 1)
        L = ["  \\node[anchor=west,font=\\small] at (0,%.2f) {%s};" % (y0 + 2.35, label)]
        for j, k in enumerate(keys):
            h = counter.get(k, 0) * scale
            if h:
                L.append("  \\fill[%s!35,draw=%s] (%.3f,%.2f) rectangle (%.3f,%.2f);"
                         % (colour, colour, j * w + 0.06, y0, (j + 1) * w - 0.06, y0 + h))
            if len(keys) <= 24 or k % 5 == 0:
                L.append("  \\node[font=\\tiny,anchor=north] at (%.3f,%.2f) {$%+d$};"
                         % ((j + 0.5) * w, y0 - 0.06, k))
        L.append("  \\draw[black!45] (0,%.2f) -- (11.6,%.2f);" % (y0, y0))
        return L
    fd = collections.Counter(r["fork"] - r["fuse"] for r in folds)
    ed = collections.Counter()
    for _, _, _, _, ds in exes:
        ed.update(ds)
    out = ["% generated by make_tables.py",
           "\\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm]"]
    out += bars(fd, "cDiv", 0, 2.0 / max(fd.values()),
                "deposited structures, %d words" % sum(fd.values()))
    out += bars(ed, "cFuse", -3.6, 2.0 / max(ed.values()),
                "compiled functions, %d words" % sum(ed.values()))
    out.append("\\end{tikzpicture}")
    return "\n".join(out)


def main():
    codons, n_exact = codon_table()
    (HERE / "tab_codons.tex").write_text(codons + "\n")
    (HERE / "tab_letters.tex").write_text(letters_table() + "\n")
    folds, frows = folds_table()
    (HERE / "tab_folds.tex").write_text(folds + "\n")
    exes, erows = exe_table()
    (HERE / "tab_exe.tex").write_text(exes + "\n")
    mt, word, regions = mtco1_table()
    (HERE / "tab_mtco1.tex").write_text(mt + "\n")
    (HERE / "dat_hist.tex").write_text(hist(frows, erows) + "\n")
    print("exact boxes", n_exact)

content.text:
Done. Twenty pages, clean build, PDF beside the source and in `ig-docs/pdfs/`. Two commits: `22e5a50` in Vox, `a5744966`'s successor in ig-docs.

Everything is now generated by `make_tables.py` from canonical sources — the residue-to-mark map and the sixty-four codons out of Vox's `genetic_table.rs`, every word, pairing and verdict out of the `vox` binary. No count in the paper is hand-typed. What's in it: all sixty-four codons with the letter each emits and its box computed exact or split from the values rather than looked up; the twelve letters with axis, codons and the chemistry of each operation; the whole 226-letter mt-co1 word with its six answered regions and the eleven divisions left standing; every structure of the fold sweep with counts, regions and reading; the executable lane; and the signed difference across both corpora value by value.

Three things worth your attention.

Vox's pairing was wrong on unbalanced words. It gave up when fork and fuse counts differed and reported every fork and every fuse unmatched — seventeen and six on mt-co1, where the surplus lemma says eleven and none. mOMonadOS's `pair_cyclic` had it right. Fixed to read from the least-balance index; verdicts are identical across the whole protein sweep and across ls, dash and gzip. `vox pairs <word>` now prints the pairing, and `vox rna --dialect mito` reads a mitochondrial gene from the command line.

The fold corpus has a duplicate: `protein_coords.pdb` deposits one nine-letter chain twelve times, and those were eleven of the twenty-one ill-typed readings. The table carries a chain-multiplicity column and both tallies, sixty-five as swept and fifty-four distinct.

The old executable row, 8/261/314/1, I could not reproduce from any binary on this machine, and nothing in the notes records what produced it. It is replaced by four binaries measured now: 5942 functions by recursive descent, 988 closing, 1849 open, 3105 null, and not one ill-typed — which is a sharper result than the row it replaces, since a compiler never emits a merge without a branch and a ribosome does.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Side-on section of the horn torus, for this manuscript.

A dedicated copy. The geometry is plotter3's and is not re-derived here; what
this file owns is everything that is a decision about a printed page rather than
about the object — the palette on a white field, which labels survive at column
width, where they sit so they do not land on the marks they name, and limits
tight enough that the section is not scaled down inside its own empty frame.

Those are manuscript decisions. Making them inside the shared plotter meant one
paper's page was silently setting the defaults for every other caller of it,
which is why this is a copy and not another flag.

    python3 horn_side_fig.py [-o horn_side.pdf]
"""

import argparse, os
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ─── Constants ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
R = 2.0; r_split = 1.0; sqrt2 = np.sqrt(2); sqrt3 = np.sqrt(3)
phi = (1 + np.sqrt(5)) / 2; inv_phi = 1 / phi; LR = R / 2

EVALT = np.array([1.0, 1.0, 0.0]); EVALF = np.array([1.0, -0.5, sqrt3/2])
EVALI = np.array([1.0, -0.5, -sqrt3/2])
tG = np.arccos(inv_phi)

# ─── Colour palette ─────────────────────────────────────────────
GREEN  = '#009E73'; BLUE   = '#0072B2'; GOLD   = '#E69F00'
ORANGE = '#E69F00'; PURPLE = '#CC79A7'; CYAN   = '#56B4E9'
GREY   = '#888888'; SLATE  = '#9AA7B4'
RED    = '#D55E00'

# INK is the foreground and PAPER the background. They were named WHITE and
# DARK, which is a statement about one theme rather than about their role, and
# that naming is why every one of the ~35 sites below had to mean 'dark'. A
# figure bound for a printed page needs black on nothing; the same geometry
# needs white on near-black on a screen. Same drawing, two bindings.
INK, PAPER = 'white', '#0a0a0a'
# A label sits ON the drawing, so it needs a background even where the FIGURE
# has none. In print the figure is transparent and rides the page, but a
# transparent label box puts glyphs straight on top of the lines they annotate.
# LABEL_BG is the page, not the figure.
LABEL_BG = '#0a0a0a'
TRANSPARENT = False


def set_theme(theme: str) -> None:
    """Bind the foreground and background for the requested theme.

    'print' is black on nothing: the figure carries no background of its own and
    sits on whatever page includes it. 'dark' is the screen theme and remains
    the default, so nothing that already calls this script changes.
    """
    # GREY and SLATE carry the construction lines and the lobe outlines. Both
    # were chosen to sit just above a near-black field, so on white they drop
    # almost to nothing and the construction the figure exists to show goes
    # missing. The hues stay; only the value moves.
    global INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT, GREY, SLATE, LABEL_BG
    if theme == "print":
        INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT = 'black', 'none', True
        LABEL_BG = 'white'
        GREY, SLATE = '#555555', '#5A6672'
    else:
        INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT = 'white', '#0a0a0a', False
        LABEL_BG = '#0a0a0a'
        GREY, SLATE = '#888888', '#9AA7B4' 

# bbox_inches crops rather than rescales, so the saved PDF is ~372pt wide and a
# declared point IS a page point. These are true sizes against 10pt body text.
GLYPH_PT = 15
LABEL_PT = 9

theta = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 500)

def horn_xy(t):
    """The horn torus's equatorial curve, gamma(t).

    gamma(0) = (2R, 0) is the OUTER equator. The horn is gamma(pi) = (0,0), the
    pinch, where the hole closes. Labelling gamma(0) 'horn(0)' therefore printed
    the word horn at the point furthest from it, on the far side of the figure
    from the pinch it names.
    """
    return np.array([(R+R*np.cos(t))*np.cos(t), (R+R*np.cos(t))*np.sin(t)])

def horn_tube_cross_section_xz():
    left_x = -R + R*np.cos(theta); left_z = R*np.sin(theta)
    right_x = R + R*np.cos(theta); right_z = R*np.sin(theta)
    return left_x, left_z, right_x, right_z


def build_three_view(output_path, dpi=300, fmt='png', title=None, views=(1, 2, 3)):
    """Build the orthographic figure, keeping only the requested views.

    All three are always drawn, because the draw code for each is written
    against its own axes and splitting it would be a larger change than the
    selection is worth. The unwanted axes are removed before the layout is
    computed, so what is saved is a figure of exactly the requested width.

    Selection exists because three panels at 30 inches wide are illegible once
    scaled into a text column: the labels survive the vector export and die on
    the page. One view at page width reads.
    """
    matplotlib.use('Agg')
    fig, (ax1, ax2, ax3) = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(30, 10))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(PAPER)

    for ax in (ax1, ax2, ax3):
        ax.set_facecolor(PAPER); ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.tick_params(colors=INK)
        for s in ax.spines.values():
            s.set_color(INK)
        ax.grid(True, ls='--', alpha=0.1)

    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # VIEW 1 — SIDE-ON (xz plane, y=0)
    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ax1.set_title('VIEW 1: Side-On (xz plane, y=0)',
                  color=INK, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=12)

    left_x, left_z, right_x, right_z = horn_tube_cross_section_xz()
    ax1.plot(left_x, left_z, color='#5a659c', lw=2.5, alpha=0.9)
    ax1.plot(right_x, right_z, color='#5a659c', lw=2.5, alpha=0.9)
    ax1.fill(left_x, left_z, color='#5a659c', alpha=0.08)
    ax1.fill(right_x, right_z, color='#5a659c', alpha=0.08)
    ax1.scatter([-R, R], [0, 0], color='#5a659c', s=40, zorder=8, marker='o', alpha=0.6)

    # λ_C split shell
    ax1.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=ORANGE, ls='--', lw=2)
    ax1.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta)*0.5, color=ORANGE, ls=':', lw=1, alpha=0.35)

    # Evaluator sphere circle
    ax1.plot(1 + r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=BLUE, ls='--', lw=2)

    # FFUSE3 coupler
    ax1.plot([0, 2], [0, 0], color=INK, lw=3)

    # Key nodes
    ax1.scatter(0, 0, color=GOLD, s=280, zorder=10, edgecolors=INK, lw=1.5)
    ax1.scatter(2, 0, color=BLUE, s=160, zorder=10, edgecolors=INK, lw=1)
    ax1.scatter(1, 0, color=BLUE, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax1.scatter(1, sqrt3/2, color=RED, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax1.scatter(1, -sqrt3/2, color=RED, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax1.scatter(LR, 0, color=INK, s=70, zorder=10, marker='s',
                edgecolors=INK, facecolors='none', lw=1.5)
    ax1.scatter(4, 0, color=PURPLE, s=120, zorder=9, marker='D',
                edgecolors=INK, lw=1, alpha=0.8)

    # Labels with background boxes
    bbox = dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor='none', pad=2.5, alpha=0.92)
    # The centre of this panel carries the coupler, two circles and five nodes
    # inside two units. A label placed next to its node either lands on a line
    # or its background box cuts one. So the crowded labels stand OUTSIDE the
    # construction and reach back with a leader: nothing is covered, and which
    # glyph names which node stays unambiguous.
    def lead(x, y, tx, ty, glyph, colour, size=None):
        ax1.annotate(glyph, xy=(x, y), xytext=(tx, ty),
                     color=colour, fontsize=size or GLYPH_PT, fontweight='bold',
                     ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox, zorder=14,
                     arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=colour, lw=0.9,
                                     alpha=0.75, shrinkA=3, shrinkB=6))

    lead(0, 0,      -0.95,  1.35, r'⊙', GOLD)
    # The horn IS the pinch. The word belongs here, not out at gamma(0).
    lead(0, 0,      -2.55, -1.45, 'horn = pinch', PURPLE, LABEL_PT)
    lead(2, 0,       2.95,  1.15, r'∋', BLUE)
    lead(LR, 0,      1.05, -1.62, '⊤',  BLUE)
    lead(1,  sqrt3/2, 2.30,  1.95, r'⊥', RED)
    lead(1, -sqrt3/2, 0.05, -1.95, r'⊞', RED)
    lead(4, 0,       4.15, -1.72, 'γ(0) equator', PURPLE, LABEL_PT)

    # Evaluator A₂ triangle fill and edges
    tri_xz = np.array([[1, 0], [1, sqrt3/2], [1, -sqrt3/2]])
    ax1.fill(tri_xz[:,0], tri_xz[:,1], color=GREEN, alpha=0.15, zorder=5)
    for i in range(3):
        j = (i+1)%3
        ax1.plot([tri_xz[i,0], tri_xz[j,0]], [tri_xz[i,1], tri_xz[j,1]],
                 color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.8)

    # Distance chords
    ax1.plot([0, 1], [0, 0], color='#aaffcc', ls=':', lw=1.5)
    # Four chord labels inside one shell radius. On screen they are readable at
    # full width; at column width they overlap each other and the pinch label,
    # so print keeps the one the section is about and drops the rest.
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax1.text(0.5, -0.2, r'$\sqrt{2}$', color=GREEN, fontsize=11,
                 fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox)
        ax1.text(0.5, sqrt3/4-0.05, r'$\sqrt{3}$', color=GREEN, fontsize=11,
                 fontweight='bold', bbox=bbox)
        ax1.text(1.0, -0.15, '2', color=CYAN, fontsize=12,
                 fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox)
    ax1.text(-1.28, 0.32, r'$\lambda_C$', color=ORANGE, fontsize=LABEL_PT,
             fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox)

    # Syzygy axis
    ax1.plot([0, 4.2], [0, 0], color=PURPLE, ls='--', lw=2, alpha=0.6)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax1.text(3.05, 0.42, 'syzygy axis', color=PURPLE, fontsize=8, alpha=0.8, bbox=bbox)

    # A₂ roots on outer equator (side view: project to x-axis)
    a2_angles = [0, 2*np.pi/3, 4*np.pi/3]
    a2_pts_xz = [(horn_xy(ang)[0], 0.0) for ang in a2_angles]
    for i, (px, pz) in enumerate(a2_pts_xz):
        offset = 0.35 if i == 0 else -0.35
        ax1.scatter(px, offset, color=GREEN, s=80, zorder=8)
        if not TRANSPARENT:
            ax1.text(px, offset+0.2, ['n₊=+1','n₋','n₋'][i],
                     color=GREEN, fontsize=7, fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox)
    for i in range(3):
        j = (i+1)%3
        ax1.plot([a2_pts_xz[i][0], a2_pts_xz[j][0]],
                 [a2_pts_xz[i][1], a2_pts_xz[j][1]],
                 color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.3, zorder=3)

    # φ-tangent loci
    phi_xz = horn_xy(tG)
    ax1.scatter(phi_xz[0], 0, color=INK, s=90, zorder=11,
                edgecolors=GOLD, lw=1.5)
    ax1.scatter(horn_xy(-tG)[0], 0, color=INK, s=90, zorder=11,
                edgecolors=GOLD, lw=1.5)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax1.text(phi_xz[0]+0.15, 0.25, r'$\phi$-tangent', color=INK,
                 fontsize=7, alpha=0.9, bbox=bbox)

    # UCFm constants for side view. Screen chrome: on a page they crowd the frame
    # corner and say nothing the caption cannot, so print omits them.
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ucfm_side = r"$\alpha^{-1}=137.035999$" + "\n" + r"$m_p/m_e=1836.152$"
        ax1.text(-5.2, 4.8, ucfm_side, color=INK, fontsize=8,
                 ha='left', va='top',
                 bbox=dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor=GOLD, alpha=0.9, pad=4))
    # The section lives in x∈[-4,4.6], z∈[-2.4,2.4]. The screen view pads it to a
    # square that is mostly empty; on a page that empty field is what gets scaled
    # and the geometry shrinks inside it.
    if TRANSPARENT:
        ax1.set_xlim(-4.6, 5.4); ax1.set_ylim(-2.8, 2.8)
    else:
        ax1.set_xlim(-5.5, 6.0); ax1.set_ylim(-5.5, 5.5)
    ax1.set_xlabel('x', color=INK); ax1.set_ylabel('z', color=INK)

    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # VIEW 2 — TOP-DOWN (xy plane, z=0)
    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ax2.set_title('VIEW 2: Top-Down (xy plane, z=0)',
                  color=INK, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=12)

    ax2.plot(2*R*np.cos(theta), 2*R*np.sin(theta), color='#5a659c', lw=2.5, alpha=0.35)
    horn_xy_pts = np.array([horn_xy(t) for t in theta])
    ax2.plot(horn_xy_pts[:,0], horn_xy_pts[:,1], color=SLATE, lw=2, alpha=0.45)

    ax2.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=ORANGE, ls='--', lw=2)
    ax2.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta)*0.5, color=ORANGE, ls=':', lw=1, alpha=0.35)
    ax2.plot(1 + r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=BLUE, ls='--', lw=2)
    ax2.plot([0, 2], [0, 0], color=INK, lw=3)    # Nodes
    ax2.scatter(0, 0, color=GOLD, s=280, zorder=10, edgecolors=INK, lw=1.5)
    ax2.scatter(2, 0, color=BLUE, s=160, zorder=10, edgecolors=INK, lw=1)
    ax2.scatter(1, 1, color=BLUE, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax2.scatter(1, -0.5, color=RED, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax2.scatter(LR, 0, color=INK, s=70, zorder=10, marker='s',
                edgecolors=INK, facecolors='none', lw=1.5)
    ax2.scatter(*horn_xy(0), color=PURPLE, s=120, zorder=9, marker='D',
                edgecolors=INK, lw=1, alpha=0.8)

    # Labels
    bbox2 = dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor='none', pad=2.5, alpha=0.92)
    # As in the side panel: the labelled nodes sit inside two units of each
    # other, so the labels stand outside the rings and lead back.
    def lead2(x, y, tx, ty, glyph, colour, size=None):
        ax2.annotate(glyph, xy=(x, y), xytext=(tx, ty),
                     color=colour, fontsize=size or GLYPH_PT, fontweight='bold',
                     ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox2, zorder=14,
                     arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=colour, lw=0.9,
                                     alpha=0.75, shrinkA=3, shrinkB=6))

    lead2(0, 0,   -1.55,  1.15, r'⊙', GOLD)
    lead2(0, 0,   -2.30, -1.75, 'horn = pinch', PURPLE, LABEL_PT)
    lead2(2, 0,    2.55,  1.70, r'∋', BLUE)
    lead2(1, 1,    0.15,  2.35, '⊤',  BLUE)
    lead2(1, -0.5, 1.95, -2.05, r'⊥', RED)
    lead2(*horn_xy(0), horn_xy(0)[0]-0.45, horn_xy(0)[1]-1.30, 'γ(0) equator',
          PURPLE, LABEL_PT)

    # A₂ roots on outer equator
    root0 = (4, 0); root1 = (4*np.cos(2*np.pi/3), 4*np.sin(2*np.pi/3))
    root2 = (4*np.cos(4*np.pi/3), 4*np.sin(4*np.pi/3))
    for rpt in [root0, root1, root2]:
        ax2.scatter(*rpt, color=GREEN, s=80, zorder=8)
    for (x1,y1),(x2,y2) in [(root0,root1),(root1,root2),(root2,root0)]:
        ax2.plot([x1,x2],[y1,y2], color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.5)

    for pt, lbl, ang in [(root0, 'n₊=+1', 0), (root1, 'n₋', 2*np.pi/3),
                          (root2, 'n₋', 4*np.pi/3)]:
        rr = 4 + (0.52 if TRANSPARENT else 0.55)
        dy = 0.42 if (TRANSPARENT and ang == 0) else 0.0
        ax2.text(rr*np.cos(ang), rr*np.sin(ang) + dy, lbl,
                 color=GREEN, fontsize=LABEL_PT if TRANSPARENT else 7,
                 fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox2)

    # A₂ triangle (collapsed to line in xy)
    ax2.plot([1, 1], [1, -0.5], color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.8)
    # A three-line note inside the shell, on top of four chord labels and the
    # pinch. What it says belongs in the caption.
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.text(0.85, 0.25, 'A₂ triangle\n(collapsed\nto line in xy)',
                 color=GREEN, fontsize=6, ha='center', bbox=bbox2)

    # Distance annotations
    ax2.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color='#aaffcc', ls=':', lw=1.5)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.text(0.4, 0.55, r'$\sqrt{2}$', color=GREEN, fontsize=11,
                 fontweight='bold', bbox=bbox2)
        ax2.text(0.55, 0.25, r'$\sqrt{3}$ (3D)', color=GREEN, fontsize=11,
                 fontweight='bold', bbox=bbox2)
        ax2.text(1.0, -0.2, '2', color=CYAN, fontsize=12,
                 fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox2)
    ax2.text(-0.72, -0.86, r'$\lambda_C$', color=ORANGE, fontsize=LABEL_PT,
             fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox2)

    # Syzygy axis
    ax2.plot([0, 4], [0, 0], color=PURPLE, ls='--', lw=2, alpha=0.6)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.text(2.1, 0.35, 'syzygy axis', color=PURPLE, fontsize=8,
                 alpha=0.8, bbox=bbox2)

    # φ-tangent loci
    phi_plus = horn_xy(tG); phi_minus = horn_xy(-tG)
    for pt in [phi_plus, phi_minus]:
        ax2.scatter(*pt, color=INK, s=90, zorder=11, edgecolors=GOLD, lw=1.5)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.text(phi_plus[0]+0.2, phi_plus[1]+0.15, r'$\phi$-tangent',
                 color=INK, fontsize=7, bbox=bbox2)

    # 16 poloidal rings
    for i in range(16):
        u = i/16*2*np.pi; rc = np.array([R*np.cos(u), R*np.sin(u)])
        ax2.plot([(R-r_split)*rc[0]/R, (R+r_split)*rc[0]/R],
                 [(R-r_split)*rc[1]/R, (R+r_split)*rc[1]/R],
                 color='#5a659c', lw=0.4, alpha=0.10)

    # UCFm constants. Derived quantities belong to the caption; in the frame
    # corner they are chrome, so print omits them.
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ucfm_top = r"Gear ratio = 4" + "\n" + r"$m_\tau/m_e = 3476.785$" + "\n" + r"$\pi$ (curvature)"
        ax2.text(-5.2, 4.8, ucfm_top, color=INK, fontsize=8,
                 ha='left', va='top',
                 bbox=dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor=GOLD, alpha=0.9, pad=4))

    if TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.set_xlim(-4.9, 5.0); ax2.set_ylim(-4.5, 4.5)
    else:
        ax2.set_xlim(-5.5, 5.5); ax2.set_ylim(-5.5, 5.5)
    ax2.set_xlabel('x', color=INK); ax2.set_ylabel('y', color=INK)

    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # VIEW 3 — FACE-ON ORTHO (yz plane, x=0)
    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ax3.set_title('VIEW 3: Face-On Ortho (yz plane, x=0)',
                  color=INK, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=12)

    # Torus lobes: left (y=-2) and right (y=+2) circles
    left_lobe_y = -R + R*np.cos(theta); left_lobe_z = R*np.sin(theta)
    right_lobe_y = R + R*np.cos(theta); right_lobe_z = R*np.sin(theta)

    ax3.plot(left_lobe_y, left_lobe_z, color='#5a659c', lw=2.5, alpha=0.9, label='Left Lobe')
    ax3.plot(right_lobe_y, right_lobe_z, color='#5a659c', lw=2.5, alpha=0.9, label='Right Lobe')
    ax3.fill(left_lobe_y, left_lobe_z, color='#5a659c', alpha=0.08)
    ax3.fill(right_lobe_y, right_lobe_z, color='#5a659c', alpha=0.08)
    ax3.scatter([-R, R], [0, 0], color='#5a659c', s=40, zorder=8, alpha=0.6)
    ax3.text(-R, -2.4, 'Left Lobe (y=-2)', color='#5a659c', fontsize=8,
             ha='center', bbox=bbox2)
    ax3.text(R, -2.4, 'Right Lobe (y=+2)', color='#5a659c', fontsize=8,
             ha='center', bbox=bbox2)

    # Evaluator / Bloch / FFUSE3 sphere — single compound circle with layered styling
    # Instead of 3 identical overlapping circles, use a single thick circle with
    # a dash-dot-dash pattern that conveys all three roles
    ax3.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=BLUE, lw=3,
             alpha=0.5, label='Evaluator / Bloch / ∋ sphere (r=1)')
    # Inner ring for depth
    ax3.plot(r_split*0.92*np.cos(theta), r_split*0.92*np.sin(theta),
             color=ORANGE, ls='--', lw=1, alpha=0.4)
    ax3.fill(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=BLUE, alpha=0.06)    # Center pinch
    ax3.scatter(0, 0, color=GOLD, s=280, zorder=15, edgecolors=INK, lw=1.5)
    ax3.text(0, -0.4, r'$\odot$ pinch / Bloch-∋ overlap', color=INK,
             fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox2)

    # Evaluator A₂ triangle nodes in yz projection
    ev_y = [EVALT[1], EVALF[1], EVALI[1]]
    ev_z = [EVALT[2], EVALF[2], EVALI[2]]

    ax3.scatter(ev_y[0], ev_z[0], color=BLUE, s=140, zorder=18,
                edgecolors=INK, lw=1.5)
    ax3.scatter(ev_y[1], ev_z[1], color=RED, s=140, zorder=18,
                edgecolors=INK, lw=1.5)
    ax3.scatter(ev_y[2], ev_z[2], color=RED, s=140, zorder=18,
                edgecolors=INK, lw=1.5)

    # A₂ evaluator triangle fill and edges
    ax3.fill(ev_y, ev_z, color=GREEN, alpha=0.18, zorder=12)
    for i in range(3):
        j = (i+1)%3
        ax3.plot([ev_y[i], ev_y[j]], [ev_z[i], ev_z[j]],
                 color=GREEN, lw=2.0, alpha=0.9, zorder=14)

    # Labels for evaluator nodes
    ax3.text(ev_y[0]+0.2, ev_z[0], '⊤', color=BLUE, fontsize=8,
             fontweight='bold', va='center', bbox=bbox2)
    ax3.text(ev_y[1]-0.2, ev_z[1]+0.2, r'⊥', color=RED,
             fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', ha='right', bbox=bbox2)
    ax3.text(ev_y[2]-0.2, ev_z[2]-0.2, r'⊞', color=RED,
             fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', ha='right', bbox=bbox2)

    # UCFm constants for face-on view
    ucfm_face = r"$\sin^2\theta_W = 3/13 = 0.230769$" + "\n" + r"$m_\mu/m_e = 206.769$"
    ax3.text(-5.2, 4.8, ucfm_face, color=INK, fontsize=8,
             ha='left', va='top',
             bbox=dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor=GOLD, alpha=0.9, pad=4))

    ax3.set_xlim(-5.5, 5.5); ax3.set_ylim(-5.5, 5.5)
    ax3.set_xlabel('y', color=INK); ax3.set_ylabel('z', color=INK)

    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # SAVE
    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    if title:
        fig.suptitle(title, color=INK, fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

    for n, ax in ((1, ax1), (2, ax2), (3, ax3)):
        if n not in views:
            fig.delaxes(ax)
    # Font sizes are in points and the figure is placed at a fixed width, so the
    # only lever on apparent type size is the panel's own inches: a 10-inch panel
    # scaled into a text column takes its 9pt labels down to about 2pt. Print
    # halves the panel, which doubles the type at the same placed width.
    # bbox_inches crops to the drawn content, which is roughly a third of the
    # declared figure width because the axes carry wide empty margins. So the
    # saved file is much narrower than the panel, and including it at \linewidth
    # MAGNIFIES it — a 7-inch panel cropped to 186pt and blown up to a 390pt
    # column took 8pt labels to about 17pt. The panel is therefore sized so the
    # cropped result lands near column width and is placed at 1:1, which is the
    # only arrangement in which the declared point sizes mean what they say.
    panel = 15 if TRANSPARENT else 10
    fig.set_size_inches(panel * len(views), panel)
    if TRANSPARENT:
        # The panel title repeats the caption on a page and is the one label
        # guaranteed to collide with the plot at column width.
        for ax in fig.axes:
            ax.set_title('')

    plt.tight_layout(pad=2.0)
    plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=dpi, facecolor=PAPER, edgecolor='none',
                bbox_inches='tight', transparent=TRANSPARENT)
    fsize = os.path.getsize(output_path)
    print(f"✅ Saved '{output_path}' ({fsize} bytes, {fsize/1024:.1f} KB, {fmt.upper()})")
    print(f"   View 1 (Side-On): kidney-bean lobes in xz plane ✓")
    print(f"   View 2 (Top-Down): equatorial rings in xy plane ✓")
    print(f"   View 3 (Face-On): side-by-side lobes + evaluator triangle on circle ✓")
    plt.close(fig)
    return output_path


def cli():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='Side-on section for the sic_moduli_conductor manuscript')
    parser.add_argument('--output', '-o',
                        default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'horn_side.pdf'),
                        help='Output path')
    parser.add_argument('--dpi', type=int, default=300, help='Resolution (default: 300)')
    parser.add_argument('--format', '-f', choices=['png','svg','pdf'], default='pdf',
                        help='Output format (default: png)')
    parser.add_argument('--title', '-t', default=None, help='Figure title (suptitle)')
    parser.add_argument('--theme', choices=['dark', 'print'], default='print',
                        help="'dark' for screen (default), 'print' for black on "
                             "a transparent background, for inclusion in a paper")
    parser.add_argument('--views', default='1',
                        help="Which views to keep, e.g. '1' or '1,3' (default: all)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    set_theme(args.theme)
    views = tuple(int(v) for v in args.views.split(',') if v.strip())

    out = args.output
    if not out.lower().endswith(('.png','.svg','.pdf')):
        out = os.path.splitext(out)[0] + '.' + args.format

    matplotlib.use('Agg')
    build_three_view(out, dpi=args.dpi, fmt=args.format, title=args.title, views=views)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    cli()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Side-on section of the horn torus, for this manuscript.

A dedicated copy. The geometry is plotter3's and is not re-derived here; what
this file owns is everything that is a decision about a printed page rather than
about the object — the palette on a white field, which labels survive at column
width, where they sit so they do not land on the marks they name, and limits
tight enough that the section is not scaled down inside its own empty frame.

Those are manuscript decisions. Making them inside the shared plotter meant one
paper's page was silently setting the defaults for every other caller of it,
which is why this is a copy and not another flag.

    python3 horn_side_fig.py [-o horn_side.pdf]
"""

import argparse, os
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ─── Constants ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
R = 2.0; r_split = 1.0; sqrt2 = np.sqrt(2); sqrt3 = np.sqrt(3)
phi = (1 + np.sqrt(5)) / 2; inv_phi = 1 / phi; LR = R / 2

EVALT = np.array([1.0, 1.0, 0.0]); EVALF = np.array([1.0, -0.5, sqrt3/2])
EVALI = np.array([1.0, -0.5, -sqrt3/2])
tG = np.arccos(inv_phi)

# ─── Colour palette ─────────────────────────────────────────────
GREEN  = '#009E73'; BLUE   = '#0072B2'; GOLD   = '#E69F00'
ORANGE = '#E69F00'; PURPLE = '#CC79A7'; CYAN   = '#56B4E9'
GREY   = '#888888'; SLATE  = '#9AA7B4'
RED    = '#D55E00'

# INK is the foreground and PAPER the background. They were named WHITE and
# DARK, which is a statement about one theme rather than about their role, and
# that naming is why every one of the ~35 sites below had to mean 'dark'. A
# figure bound for a printed page needs black on nothing; the same geometry
# needs white on near-black on a screen. Same drawing, two bindings.
INK, PAPER = 'white', '#0a0a0a'
# A label sits ON the drawing, so it needs a background even where the FIGURE
# has none. In print the figure is transparent and rides the page, but a
# transparent label box puts glyphs straight on top of the lines they annotate.
# LABEL_BG is the page, not the figure.
LABEL_BG = '#0a0a0a'
TRANSPARENT = False


def set_theme(theme: str) -> None:
    """Bind the foreground and background for the requested theme.

    'print' is black on nothing: the figure carries no background of its own and
    sits on whatever page includes it. 'dark' is the screen theme and remains
    the default, so nothing that already calls this script changes.
    """
    # GREY and SLATE carry the construction lines and the lobe outlines. Both
    # were chosen to sit just above a near-black field, so on white they drop
    # almost to nothing and the construction the figure exists to show goes
    # missing. The hues stay; only the value moves.
    global INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT, GREY, SLATE, LABEL_BG
    if theme == "print":
        INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT = 'black', 'none', True
        LABEL_BG = 'white'
        GREY, SLATE = '#555555', '#5A6672'
    else:
        INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT = 'white', '#0a0a0a', False
        LABEL_BG = '#0a0a0a'
        GREY, SLATE = '#888888', '#9AA7B4' 

# bbox_inches crops rather than rescales, so the saved PDF is ~372pt wide and a
# declared point IS a page point. These are true sizes against 10pt body text.
GLYPH_PT = 15
LABEL_PT = 9

theta = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 500)

def horn_xy(t):
    """The horn torus's equatorial curve, gamma(t).

    gamma(0) = (2R, 0) is the OUTER equator. The horn is gamma(pi) = (0,0), the
    pinch, where the hole closes. Labelling gamma(0) 'horn(0)' therefore printed
    the word horn at the point furthest from it, on the far side of the figure
    from the pinch it names.
    """
    return np.array([(R+R*np.cos(t))*np.cos(t), (R+R*np.cos(t))*np.sin(t)])

def horn_tube_cross_section_xz():
    left_x = -R + R*np.cos(theta); left_z = R*np.sin(theta)
    right_x = R + R*np.cos(theta); right_z = R*np.sin(theta)
    return left_x, left_z, right_x, right_z


def build_three_view(output_path, dpi=300, fmt='png', title=None, views=(1, 2, 3)):
    """Build the orthographic figure, keeping only the requested views.

    All three are always drawn, because the draw code for each is written
    against its own axes and splitting it would be a larger change than the
    selection is worth. The unwanted axes are removed before the layout is
    computed, so what is saved is a figure of exactly the requested width.

    Selection exists because three panels at 30 inches wide are illegible once
    scaled into a text column: the labels survive the vector export and die on
    the page. One view at page width reads.
    """
    matplotlib.use('Agg')
    fig, (ax1, ax2, ax3) = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(30, 10))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(PAPER)

    for ax in (ax1, ax2, ax3):
        ax.set_facecolor(PAPER); ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.tick_params(colors=INK)
        for s in ax.spines.values():
            s.set_color(INK)
        ax.grid(True, ls='--', alpha=0.1)

    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # VIEW 1 — SIDE-ON (xz plane, y=0)
    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ax1.set_title('VIEW 1: Side-On (xz plane, y=0)',
                  color=INK, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=12)

    left_x, left_z, right_x, right_z = horn_tube_cross_section_xz()
    ax1.plot(left_x, left_z, color='#5a659c', lw=2.5, alpha=0.9)
    ax1.plot(right_x, right_z, color='#5a659c', lw=2.5, alpha=0.9)
    ax1.fill(left_x, left_z, color='#5a659c', alpha=0.08)
    ax1.fill(right_x, right_z, color='#5a659c', alpha=0.08)
    ax1.scatter([-R, R], [0, 0], color='#5a659c', s=40, zorder=8, marker='o', alpha=0.6)

    # λ_C split shell
    ax1.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=ORANGE, ls='--', lw=2)
    ax1.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta)*0.5, color=ORANGE, ls=':', lw=1, alpha=0.35)

    # Evaluator sphere circle
    ax1.plot(1 + r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=BLUE, ls='--', lw=2)

    # FFUSE3 coupler
    ax1.plot([0, 2], [0, 0], color=INK, lw=3)

    # Key nodes
    ax1.scatter(0, 0, color=GOLD, s=280, zorder=10, edgecolors=INK, lw=1.5)
    ax1.scatter(2, 0, color=BLUE, s=160, zorder=10, edgecolors=INK, lw=1)
    ax1.scatter(1, 0, color=BLUE, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax1.scatter(1, sqrt3/2, color=RED, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax1.scatter(1, -sqrt3/2, color=RED, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax1.scatter(LR, 0, color=INK, s=70, zorder=10, marker='s',
                edgecolors=INK, facecolors='none', lw=1.5)
    ax1.scatter(4, 0, color=PURPLE, s=120, zorder=9, marker='D',
                edgecolors=INK, lw=1, alpha=0.8)

    # Labels with background boxes
    bbox = dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor='none', pad=2.5, alpha=0.92)
    # The centre of this panel carries the coupler, two circles and five nodes
    # inside two units. A label placed next to its node either lands on a line
    # or its background box cuts one. So the crowded labels stand OUTSIDE the
    # construction and reach back with a leader: nothing is covered, and which
    # glyph names which node stays unambiguous.
    def lead(x, y, tx, ty, glyph, colour, size=None):
        ax1.annotate(glyph, xy=(x, y), xytext=(tx, ty),
                     color=colour, fontsize=size or GLYPH_PT, fontweight='bold',
                     ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox, zorder=14,
                     arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=colour, lw=0.9,
                                     alpha=0.75, shrinkA=3, shrinkB=6))

    lead(0, 0,      -0.95,  1.35, r'⊙', GOLD)
    # The horn IS the pinch. The word belongs here, not out at gamma(0).
    lead(0, 0,      -2.55, -1.45, 'horn = pinch', PURPLE, LABEL_PT)
    lead(2, 0,       2.95,  1.15, r'∋', BLUE)
    lead(LR, 0,      1.05, -1.62, '⊤',  BLUE)
    lead(1,  sqrt3/2, 2.30,  1.95, r'⊥', RED)
    lead(1, -sqrt3/2, 0.05, -1.95, r'⊞', RED)
    lead(4, 0,       4.15, -1.72, 'γ(0) equator', PURPLE, LABEL_PT)

    # Evaluator A₂ triangle fill and edges
    tri_xz = np.array([[1, 0], [1, sqrt3/2], [1, -sqrt3/2]])
    ax1.fill(tri_xz[:,0], tri_xz[:,1], color=GREEN, alpha=0.15, zorder=5)
    for i in range(3):
        j = (i+1)%3
        ax1.plot([tri_xz[i,0], tri_xz[j,0]], [tri_xz[i,1], tri_xz[j,1]],
                 color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.8)

    # Distance chords
    ax1.plot([0, 1], [0, 0], color='#aaffcc', ls=':', lw=1.5)
    # Four chord labels inside one shell radius. On screen they are readable at
    # full width; at column width they overlap each other and the pinch label,
    # so print keeps the one the section is about and drops the rest.
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax1.text(0.5, -0.2, r'$\sqrt{2}$', color=GREEN, fontsize=11,
                 fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox)
        ax1.text(0.5, sqrt3/4-0.05, r'$\sqrt{3}$', color=GREEN, fontsize=11,
                 fontweight='bold', bbox=bbox)
        ax1.text(1.0, -0.15, '2', color=CYAN, fontsize=12,
                 fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox)
    ax1.text(-1.28, 0.32, r'$\lambda_C$', color=ORANGE, fontsize=LABEL_PT,
             fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox)

    # Syzygy axis
    ax1.plot([0, 4.2], [0, 0], color=PURPLE, ls='--', lw=2, alpha=0.6)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax1.text(3.05, 0.42, 'syzygy axis', color=PURPLE, fontsize=8, alpha=0.8, bbox=bbox)

    # A₂ roots on outer equator (side view: project to x-axis)
    a2_angles = [0, 2*np.pi/3, 4*np.pi/3]
    a2_pts_xz = [(horn_xy(ang)[0], 0.0) for ang in a2_angles]
    for i, (px, pz) in enumerate(a2_pts_xz):
        offset = 0.35 if i == 0 else -0.35
        ax1.scatter(px, offset, color=GREEN, s=80, zorder=8)
        if not TRANSPARENT:
            ax1.text(px, offset+0.2, ['n₊=+1','n₋','n₋'][i],
                     color=GREEN, fontsize=7, fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox)
    for i in range(3):
        j = (i+1)%3
        ax1.plot([a2_pts_xz[i][0], a2_pts_xz[j][0]],
                 [a2_pts_xz[i][1], a2_pts_xz[j][1]],
                 color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.3, zorder=3)

    # φ-tangent loci
    phi_xz = horn_xy(tG)
    ax1.scatter(phi_xz[0], 0, color=INK, s=90, zorder=11,
                edgecolors=GOLD, lw=1.5)
    ax1.scatter(horn_xy(-tG)[0], 0, color=INK, s=90, zorder=11,
                edgecolors=GOLD, lw=1.5)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax1.text(phi_xz[0]+0.15, 0.25, r'$\phi$-tangent', color=INK,
                 fontsize=7, alpha=0.9, bbox=bbox)

    # UCFm constants for side view. Screen chrome: on a page they crowd the frame
    # corner and say nothing the caption cannot, so print omits them.
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ucfm_side = r"$\alpha^{-1}=137.035999$" + "\n" + r"$m_p/m_e=1836.152$"
        ax1.text(-5.2, 4.8, ucfm_side, color=INK, fontsize=8,
                 ha='left', va='top',
                 bbox=dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor=GOLD, alpha=0.9, pad=4))
    # The section lives in x∈[-4,4.6], z∈[-2.4,2.4]. The screen view pads it to a
    # square that is mostly empty; on a page that empty field is what gets scaled
    # and the geometry shrinks inside it.
    if TRANSPARENT:
        ax1.set_xlim(-4.6, 5.4); ax1.set_ylim(-2.8, 2.8)
    else:
        ax1.set_xlim(-5.5, 6.0); ax1.set_ylim(-5.5, 5.5)
    ax1.set_xlabel('x', color=INK); ax1.set_ylabel('z', color=INK)

    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # VIEW 2 — TOP-DOWN (xy plane, z=0)
    # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    ax2.set_title('VIEW 2: Top-Down (xy plane, z=0)',
                  color=INK, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=12)

    ax2.plot(2*R*np.cos(theta), 2*R*np.sin(theta), color='#5a659c', lw=2.5, alpha=0.35)
    horn_xy_pts = np.array([horn_xy(t) for t in theta])
    ax2.plot(horn_xy_pts[:,0], horn_xy_pts[:,1], color=SLATE, lw=2, alpha=0.45)

    ax2.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=ORANGE, ls='--', lw=2)
    ax2.plot(r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta)*0.5, color=ORANGE, ls=':', lw=1, alpha=0.35)
    ax2.plot(1 + r_split*np.cos(theta), r_split*np.sin(theta), color=BLUE, ls='--', lw=2)
    ax2.plot([0, 2], [0, 0], color=INK, lw=3)    # Nodes
    ax2.scatter(0, 0, color=GOLD, s=280, zorder=10, edgecolors=INK, lw=1.5)
    ax2.scatter(2, 0, color=BLUE, s=160, zorder=10, edgecolors=INK, lw=1)
    ax2.scatter(1, 1, color=BLUE, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax2.scatter(1, -0.5, color=RED, s=120, zorder=10)
    ax2.scatter(LR, 0, color=INK, s=70, zorder=10, marker='s',
                edgecolors=INK, facecolors='none', lw=1.5)
    ax2.scatter(*horn_xy(0), color=PURPLE, s=120, zorder=9, marker='D',
                edgecolors=INK, lw=1, alpha=0.8)

    # Labels
    bbox2 = dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor='none', pad=2.5, alpha=0.92)
    # As in the side panel: the labelled nodes sit inside two units of each
    # other, so the labels stand outside the rings and lead back.
    def lead2(x, y, tx, ty, glyph, colour, size=None):
        ax2.annotate(glyph, xy=(x, y), xytext=(tx, ty),
                     color=colour, fontsize=size or GLYPH_PT, fontweight='bold',
                     ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox2, zorder=14,
                     arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=colour, lw=0.9,
                                     alpha=0.75, shrinkA=3, shrinkB=6))

    lead2(0, 0,   -1.55,  1.15, r'⊙', GOLD)
    lead2(0, 0,   -2.30, -1.75, 'horn = pinch', PURPLE, LABEL_PT)
    lead2(2, 0,    2.55,  1.70, r'∋', BLUE)
    lead2(1, 1,    0.15,  2.35, '⊤',  BLUE)
    lead2(1, -0.5, 1.95, -2.05, r'⊥', RED)
    lead2(*horn_xy(0), horn_xy(0)[0]-0.45, horn_xy(0)[1]-1.30, 'γ(0) equator',
          PURPLE, LABEL_PT)

    # A₂ roots on outer equator
    root0 = (4, 0); root1 = (4*np.cos(2*np.pi/3), 4*np.sin(2*np.pi/3))
    root2 = (4*np.cos(4*np.pi/3), 4*np.sin(4*np.pi/3))
    for rpt in [root0, root1, root2]:
        ax2.scatter(*rpt, color=GREEN, s=80, zorder=8)
    for (x1,y1),(x2,y2) in [(root0,root1),(root1,root2),(root2,root0)]:
        ax2.plot([x1,x2],[y1,y2], color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.5)

    for pt, lbl, ang in [(root0, 'n₊=+1', 0), (root1, 'n₋', 2*np.pi/3),
                          (root2, 'n₋', 4*np.pi/3)]:
        rr = 4 + (0.52 if TRANSPARENT else 0.55)
        dy = 0.42 if (TRANSPARENT and ang == 0) else 0.0
        ax2.text(rr*np.cos(ang), rr*np.sin(ang) + dy, lbl,
                 color=GREEN, fontsize=LABEL_PT if TRANSPARENT else 7,
                 fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox2)

    # A₂ triangle (collapsed to line in xy)
    ax2.plot([1, 1], [1, -0.5], color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.8)
    # A three-line note inside the shell, on top of four chord labels and the
    # pinch. What it says belongs in the caption.
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.text(0.85, 0.25, 'A₂ triangle\n(collapsed\nto line in xy)',
                 color=GREEN, fontsize=6, ha='center', bbox=bbox2)

    # Distance annotations
    ax2.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color='#aaffcc', ls=':', lw=1.5)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.text(0.4, 0.55, r'$\sqrt{2}$', color=GREEN, fontsize=11,
                 fontweight='bold', bbox=bbox2)
        ax2.text(0.55, 0.25, r'$\sqrt{3}$ (3D)', color=GREEN, fontsize=11,
                 fontweight='bold', bbox=bbox2)
        ax2.text(1.0, -0.2, '2', color=CYAN, fontsize=12,
                 fontweight='bold', ha='center', bbox=bbox2)
    ax2.text(-0.72, -0.86, r'$\lambda_C$', color=ORANGE, fontsize=LABEL_PT,
             fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox2)

    # Syzygy axis
    ax2.plot([0, 4], [0, 0], color=PURPLE, ls='--', lw=2, alpha=0.6)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.text(2.1, 0.35, 'syzygy axis', color=PURPLE, fontsize=8,
                 alpha=0.8, bbox=bbox2)

    # φ-tangent loci
    phi_plus = horn_xy(tG); phi_minus = horn_xy(-tG)
    for pt in [phi_plus, phi_minus]:
        ax2.scatter(*pt, color=INK, s=90, zorder=11, edgecolors=GOLD, lw=1.5)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax2.text(phi_plus[0]+0.2, phi_plus[1]+0.15, r'$\phi$-tangent',
                 color=INK, fontsize=7, bbox=bbox2)

    # 16 poloidal rings

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The view down the evaluator sphere's own axis, for this manuscript.

The side-on and top-down sections both look ACROSS the syzygy axis, and in both
of them the evaluator trine is edge-on: three points on a line at x=1. This is
the third orthographic view, taken along that axis, and it is the only one in
which the trine stands as what it is, an equilateral triangle at 120 degrees
inscribed in the evaluator sphere's equator.

A dedicated copy, for the reason horn_side_fig.py is one: what it owns is the
decisions about a printed page, not the geometry, which is plotter3's.

    python3 horn_axial_fig.py [-o horn_axial.pdf] [--theme print|dark]
"""

import argparse, os
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ─── Constants, the same ones the other sections carry ──────────
R = 2.0                      # major radius, and the tube radius: a horn torus
r_split = 1.0                # lambda_C, and the evaluator sphere: r = R/2
sqrt3 = np.sqrt(3)

# The trine sits in the plane x = 1, one radius along the axis, which is where
# the evaluator sphere's equator is. Looking down x, these three are the circle's
# own 120-degree points.
EVALT = np.array([1.0, 1.0, 0.0])
EVALF = np.array([1.0, -0.5, sqrt3 / 2])
EVALI = np.array([1.0, -0.5, -sqrt3 / 2])

GREEN = '#009E73'; BLUE = '#0072B2'; GOLD = '#E69F00'
ORANGE = '#E69F00'; PURPLE = '#CC79A7'; RED = '#D55E00'
INK, PAPER = 'white', '#0a0a0a'
LABEL_BG = '#0a0a0a'
GREY, SLATE = '#888888', '#9AA7B4'
TRANSPARENT = False

GLYPH_PT = 15
LABEL_PT = 9

theta = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 720)


def set_theme(theme: str) -> None:
    global INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT, GREY, SLATE, LABEL_BG
    if theme == "print":
        INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT = 'black', 'none', True
        LABEL_BG = 'white'
        GREY, SLATE = '#555555', '#5A6672'
    else:
        INK, PAPER, TRANSPARENT = 'white', '#0a0a0a', False
        LABEL_BG = '#0a0a0a'
        GREY, SLATE = '#888888', '#9AA7B4'


def horn_silhouette():
    """The horn torus seen along x.

    The surface is ((R + R cos v) cos u, (R + R cos v) sin u, R sin v). Dropping
    x leaves (y, z) = ((R + R cos v) sin u, R sin v), so at a height z the widest
    the body reaches is R + R*sqrt(1 - (z/R)^2), and the hole has closed: the
    silhouette is one region, not an annulus, which is what makes it a horn.
    """
    z = np.linspace(-R, R, 400)
    y = R + R * np.sqrt(np.clip(1 - (z / R) ** 2, 0, 1))
    return y, z


def build(output_path, dpi=300):
    matplotlib.use('Agg')
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(15, 15) if TRANSPARENT else (10, 10))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(PAPER)
    ax.set_facecolor(PAPER); ax.set_aspect('equal')
    ax.tick_params(colors=INK)
    for s in ax.spines.values():
        s.set_color(INK)
    ax.grid(True, ls='--', alpha=0.1)

    bbox = dict(facecolor=LABEL_BG, edgecolor='none', pad=2.5, alpha=0.92)

    # ── the body, seen end-on ───────────────────────────────────
    sy, sz = horn_silhouette()
    ax.plot(sy, sz, color='#5a659c', lw=2.0, alpha=0.55)
    ax.plot(-sy, sz, color='#5a659c', lw=2.0, alpha=0.55)
    ax.fill_betweenx(sz, -sy, sy, color='#5a659c', alpha=0.05)

    # ── the two spheres, both cut on the axis, both of radius R/2 ─
    # lambda_C is centred on the pinch and the evaluator sphere one radius
    # along; along this line of sight they are concentric and the same size, so
    # they project onto ONE circle. Drawing them as two would invent a
    # separation the geometry does not have.
    ax.plot(r_split * np.cos(theta), r_split * np.sin(theta),
            color=BLUE, lw=3, alpha=0.85)
    ax.plot(r_split * np.cos(theta), r_split * np.sin(theta),
            color=ORANGE, ls=(0, (6, 6)), lw=2.2, alpha=0.95)
    ax.fill(r_split * np.cos(theta), r_split * np.sin(theta),
            color=BLUE, alpha=0.05)

    # ── the trine, standing ─────────────────────────────────────
    ev_y = [EVALT[1], EVALF[1], EVALI[1]]
    ev_z = [EVALT[2], EVALF[2], EVALI[2]]
    ax.fill(ev_y, ev_z, color=GREEN, alpha=0.16, zorder=12)
    for i in range(3):
        j = (i + 1) % 3
        ax.plot([ev_y[i], ev_y[j]], [ev_z[i], ev_z[j]],
                color=GREEN, lw=2.4, alpha=0.95, zorder=13)
    ax.scatter(ev_y[0], ev_z[0], color=BLUE, s=150, zorder=18,
               edgecolors=INK, lw=1.4)
    ax.scatter(ev_y[1], ev_z[1], color=RED, s=150, zorder=18,
               edgecolors=INK, lw=1.4)
    ax.scatter(ev_y[2], ev_z[2], color=RED, s=150, zorder=18,
               edgecolors=INK, lw=1.4)

    # the 120 degrees, drawn rather than asserted
    for ang in (0, 2 * np.pi / 3, 4 * np.pi / 3):
        ax.plot([0, np.cos(ang)], [0, np.sin(ang)],
                color=GREEN, ls=':', lw=1.2, alpha=0.6, zorder=6)
    arc = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi / 3, 120)
    ax.plot(0.34 * np.cos(arc), 0.34 * np.sin(arc), color=GREEN, lw=1.2, alpha=0.8)
    ax.text(0.34 * np.cos(np.pi / 3) + 0.13, 0.34 * np.sin(np.pi / 3) + 0.10,
            r'$120^\circ$', color=GREEN, fontsize=LABEL_PT, fontweight='bold',
            ha='left', va='center', bbox=bbox)

    def lead(x, y, tx, ty, glyph, colour, size=None):
        ax.annotate(glyph, xy=(x, y), xytext=(tx, ty),
                    color=colour, fontsize=size or GLYPH_PT, fontweight='bold',
                    ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox, zorder=20,
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=colour, lw=0.9,
                                    alpha=0.75, shrinkA=3, shrinkB=6))

    lead(ev_y[0], ev_z[0], 1.62, 0.30, r'⊤', BLUE)
    lead(ev_y[1], ev_z[1], -1.50, 1.42, r'⊥', RED)
    lead(ev_y[2], ev_z[2], -1.50, -1.42, r'⊞', RED)

    # ── the axis, end-on ────────────────────────────────────────
    # Everything that stands ON the axis lands on one point here: the pinch at
    # x=0, the fuse at x=2, the coupler between them, and the outer equator
    # gamma(0) at x=4. That coincidence is the content of this view.
    ax.scatter(0, 0, s=430, facecolors='none', edgecolors=GOLD, lw=2.0, zorder=15)
    ax.scatter(0, 0, color=GOLD, s=150, zorder=16, edgecolors=INK, lw=1.2)
    lead(0, 0, -0.10, 2.32, r'⊙ · ∋ · γ(0), on the axis', GOLD, LABEL_PT)

    # ── the A2 roots, edge-on here, which is the trade ──────────
    # In the top-down section these three stand at 120 degrees on the outer
    # equator and the trine collapses to a segment. Along the axis it is the
    # other way about, and the roots fall on one line.
    for ang, lbl in ((0, 'n₊=+1'), (2 * np.pi / 3, 'n₋'), (4 * np.pi / 3, 'n₋')):
        py = 4 * np.sin(ang)
        ax.scatter(py, 0, color=GREEN, s=85, zorder=9)
        ax.text(py, -0.34, lbl, color=GREEN, fontsize=LABEL_PT - 1,
                fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox)
    ax.plot([4 * np.sin(2 * np.pi / 3), 4 * np.sin(4 * np.pi / 3)], [0, 0],
            color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.30, zorder=4)

    ax.text(-3.05, 1.62, 'evaluator sphere equator\nand $\\lambda_C$, one circle',
            color=BLUE, fontsize=LABEL_PT, ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox)
    ax.annotate('', xy=(-0.92, 0.40), xytext=(-2.35, 1.40),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=BLUE, lw=0.9, alpha=0.7))

    ax.set_xlim(-4.7, 4.7); ax.set_ylim(-3.1, 3.1)
    ax.set_xlabel('y', color=INK); ax.set_ylabel('z', color=INK)
    if not TRANSPARENT:
        ax.set_title('Down the evaluator axis (yz projection, looking along x)',
                     color=INK, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=12)

    plt.tight_layout(pad=2.0)
    plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=dpi, facecolor=PAPER, edgecolor='none',
                bbox_inches='tight', transparent=TRANSPARENT)
    fsize = os.path.getsize(output_path)
    print(f"saved {output_path} ({fsize/1024:.1f} KB)")
    plt.close(fig)
    return output_path


def cli():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='The axial view for the sic_moduli_conductor manuscript')
    p.add_argument('--output', '-o',
                   default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'horn_axial.pdf'))
    p.add_argument('--dpi', type=int, default=300)
    p.add_argument('--theme', choices=['dark', 'print'], default='print')
    a = p.parse_args()
    set_theme(a.theme)
    build(a.output, dpi=a.dpi)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    cli()

    ax.plot(0.34 * np.cos(arc), 0.34 * np.sin(arc), color=GREEN, lw=1.2, alpha=0.8)

    lead(ev_y[1], ev_z[1], -1.50, 1.42, r'⊥', RED)

                fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox)

            color=GREEN, lw=2, alpha=0.30, zorder=4)

            color=BLUE, fontsize=LABEL_PT, ha='center', va='center', bbox=bbox)

                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=BLUE, lw=0.9, alpha=0.7))

    plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=dpi, facecolor=PAPER, edgecolor='none',
                bbox_inches='tight', transparent=TRANSPARENT)
    fsize = os.path.getsize(output_path)
    print(f"saved {output_path} ({fsize/1024:.1f} KB)")
    plt.close(fig)
    return output_path


def cli():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='The axial view for the sic_moduli_conductor manuscript')
    p.add_argument('--output', '-o',
                   default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'horn_axial.pdf'))
    p.add_argument('--dpi', type=int, default=300)
    p.add_argument('--theme', choices=['dark', 'print'], default='print')
    a = p.parse_args()
    set_theme(a.theme)
    build(a.output, dpi=a.dpi)

content.text:
The axial view is in, Figure 4, built with `ltx` and committed as `1fa1ac48`.

The generator's old View 3 was a face-on section at x=0, which is not this: the trine sits in the plane x=1, so looking down the syzygy axis is what makes it stand. `figs/horn_axial_fig.py` is a dedicated generator beside `horn_side_fig.py`, and what it draws is the trine as an equilateral triangle at 120° inscribed in the evaluator sphere's equator, with the angle drawn rather than asserted.

Three things the view puts together that neither section could. λ_C and the evaluator sphere project onto one circle — both radius R/2, both centred on the axis, so along this line of sight they are concentric and the same size, and drawing them as two would invent a separation the geometry does not have; they carry one circle in two strokes. Everything the axis carries lands on the single point at the centre: the pinch at x=0, the fuse at x=2, the coupler between them, γ(0) at x=2R, and the n₊=+1 root, which is at angle zero and therefore on the line of sight. And the two remaining roots fall on the horizontal line, so the A₂ root triangle is edge-on in exactly the view where the trine stands, and the trine is edge-on in the view where the roots stand — the two figures trade, which the caption now says. The outline is the horn torus end-on, widest at z=0 and closing to the tube's width at z=±R, one region rather than an annulus because the hole has shut.

The first build placed the figure at about 2pt type: a fifteen-inch panel cropped and scaled into a 390pt column. It is sized now so the crop lands near column width and a declared nine-point label prints as nine points. The Unity paragraph's reference to the geometric realization now includes it.
